sources.title: Job Objects — Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn
sources.released_version_or_commit: Live Microsoft Learn page; last updated 2025-07-14
sources.locator: Creating Jobs; Managing Processes in Jobs; managing a process tree; closing a job object handle
sources.observed_operation: Opened the exact page and inspected process association, CreateProcess inheritance exceptions, breakaway, termination, nested-job and last-handle close behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: CreateJobObject starts empty; AssignProcessToJobObject associates a process. CreateProcess descendants normally inherit except Win32_Process.Create; breakaway flags change this. Nested jobs were added in Windows 8. KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE terminates members when the last handle closes.
sources.applicability: Checks the proposed task-specific Windows process boundary and F01 shutdown/reaping gap; does not prove target-host assignment capability.

sources.title: JOBOBJECT_BASIC_LIMIT_INFORMATION — Win32 apps | Microsoft Learn
sources.released_version_or_commit: Live Microsoft Learn API reference; page last updated 2022-08-23
sources.observed_operation: Opened the exact API reference and inspected limit flag definitions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: JOB_MEMORY limits the job-wide sum of committed memory and rejects commits beyond the limit; KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE terminates members when the last handle closes. This is not a host-wide memory cap.
sources.applicability: Checks the draft's Windows metric and boundary wording.

sources.title: Control Group v2 — Linux Kernel documentation 6.14
sources.locator: Memory controller: memory.current, memory.peak, memory.high, memory.max; Delegation
sources.observed_operation: Opened the version-pinned reference and inspected the accounting, peak, throttle/hard-limit and delegation sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: memory.current covers a cgroup and descendants; memory.peak tracks maximum use since creation/reset. memory.high throttles/reclaims but may be exceeded and does not invoke OOM; memory.max is the hard control but may be exceeded temporarily and can invoke OOM inside the cgroup. Controller behavior is hierarchical and delegation has permission boundaries.
sources.applicability: Checks Linux resource-accounting and conditional-enforcement claims; does not establish host availability.

sources.title: Control Group APIs and Delegation — systemd.io
sources.locator: Single-writer rule; Delegate=; controller availability and enablement
sources.observed_operation: Opened the page and inspected ownership, delegated subtree, requested-controller caveat, and manual memory-controller enablement text.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Each cgroup has a single manager. Delegate= on service/scope makes a subtree available, but the requested controllers may not be available and systemd does not itself enable them; memory must be enabled within the delegated subtree.
sources.applicability: Checks the draft's capability-detection and ownership caveats for rootless Linux execution.

sources.title: Write-Ahead Logging — SQLite
sources.locator: WAL constraints, concurrency, checkpointing, WAL-reset bug (sections 1, 2, 3, 11)
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official WAL documentation and inspected same-host constraint, single-writer, checkpoint and bug-fix sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WAL readers and writers can overlap but only one writer exists; all database processes must be on the same host; checkpoint progress can be constrained by readers. The WAL-reset bug is fixed in 3.51.3 and later, with listed backports.
sources.applicability: Checks the local embedded queue candidate and the draft's stated release floor; not a decision to use SQLite.

sources.title: PRAGMA synchronous — SQLite
sources.locator: FULL and NORMAL semantics under WAL mode
sources.observed_operation: Opened the synchronous pragma reference and compared power-loss and application-crash behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: In WAL mode NORMAL is consistent and survives application crashes, but a recently committed transaction may roll back after system/power failure. FULL adds a WAL sync after each commit to improve power-loss durability.
sources.applicability: Checks the draft's explicit durability/performance owner decision.

sources.observed_operation: Opened the official release history and located the current release, 3.53.4 entry and 3.51.3 WAL-reset fix record.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The page lists 3.54.0 dated 2026-10-09 above 3.53.4 dated 2026-07-24; it records the WAL-reset fix in 3.51.3 and later releases.
sources.applicability: Supports F03's source-record correction and confirms the draft's minimum fixed-release floor.

sources.title: Semaphore in tokio::sync — Rust docs.rs
sources.released_version_or_commit: Tokio 1.53.2 shown by the retrieved API page; latest URL is mutable
sources.locator: Semaphore fairness and acquire_many head-of-line behavior; acquire_many cancel safety
sources.observed_operation: Opened the published API reference and inspected FIFO order and large acquire_many behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Permits are given in request order; an acquire_many at the queue head can prevent a smaller acquire from completing even when the semaphore has enough permits for the smaller request. Canceling acquire_many loses queue position.
sources.applicability: Checks the semaphore comparison only; it does not establish extension-queue fairness.

sources.released_version_or_commit: Live VS Code API documentation accessed 2026-10-12
sources.observed_operation: Opened the extension API reference and inspected withProgress's progress callback and cancellation-token signature.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: withProgress receives a progress callback and CancellationToken while its operation is pending; the API is a product precedent, not a dependency or host design.
sources.applicability: Checks the draft's limited progress/cancellation precedent.
